verdict.rationale: Nothing in the evidence pack documents Fastmail blocking tracking pixels or remote images, by default or otherwise. The only related item is one community remark that Fastmail is 'up front with how the data is handled', which is a thin, non-documentary nod to transparency and does not cover the core tracking-protection capability. Jurisdiction and data-residency complaints are about hosting location, not sender tracking, so they were not weighed.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
